openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Sunday’s gate is a live Operator Manual window, a clearing fog, and a full Week 3 board — not the overnight security stack. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Own the threshold from the first breath.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for a clean inbox or a perfect admin stack to start. Fierce calm is Sunday composure when a drop window and a Week 3 board both want the first hour: charge first, body second, security skim when ready, drop ops with a steady hand, Cash App and Progressive only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Competitors may still be refreshing TNF recaps or agent-review filings; he arrives prepared for the Operator Manual window. When pressure rises, he slows the breath, names the next action, and outlasts the noise. Today is not about proving anything on the scoreboard. It is about banking competitive calm so amber, kill, buyer replies, and quiet admin have a settled operator behind them. Fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Sunday: run this after Morning Charge — box breathing first, then the body. Fog clearing outside; tempo inside before the drop window and the Week 3 board. Then news and the day.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time. Optional: Front Clips / Back Clips if you want a second RipStick move.

Gnostic operators sealed the day before opening the market of messages. A sealed morning is not empty — it is protected. Opening Bell is that seal before the drop window and the Week 3 board.

Hermetic builders lit one flame and carried it room to room rather than lighting a new candle at every door. One charged operator moves through amber, kill, and replies without restarting the self each hour.
Esoteric duelists trained the draw until speed felt like stillness. Competitive calm is that draw — fast enough for the window, quiet enough that panic never gets a grip on the hilt.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.body: “The hand of the diligent will rule, while the slothful will be put to forced labor.” (Proverbs 12:24) Solomon’s counsel for a drop Sunday is diligence without frenzy — rule the window by preparing the hand (charge + body + one security skim), then execute the ops cadence (amber, CFA clear, replies, kill) from a settled seat. Classical lore cast Solomon as one who ordered the temple watch so the work did not own the watchman. Order the Sunday the same way, so the Operator Manual window meets a ruler — not a laborer chased by the clock.
grimoire.practice: Finish Opening Bell and the 3-minute opener before any security skim or drop reply. Diligent hand first; window second.
